blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).

    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

#

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

messages.preview: The factory kicker at the pinned SHA handles `workflow_run` safely (event-agnostic liveness check + all-open-PR scan; no `github.event.workflow_run.*` payload is ever interpolated). Let me verify pari…

blocks.text:
Now I have the factory kicker logic at the pinned SHA. Analysis of how it behaves under a `workflow_run` trigger:

1. **`sm-liveness` job**: Checks if machine-sm.yml has an active run; if not, dispatches one. This is payload-independent — reads live repo state via API. Works fine under `workflow_run` trigger. ✅ This is exactly the fix for the described stall: Quality completes → kicker fires → SM idle → dispatch tick → verdict latches within seconds.

2. **`head-completeness` job**: 
   - For `push` events: scans the pushed branch only.
   - Else (schedule, workflow_dispatch, and NOW workflow_run): scans ALL open PR branches. Under `workflow_run` events, `GITHUB_REF_TYPE` is "branch" (default branch) and `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is "main"... wait, careful! For a `workflow_run` event, the workflow run executes on the default branch, so `GITHUB_REF_NAME` = "main" and `GITHUB_REF_TYPE` = "branch".

   ⚠️ **This is a real issue**: the head-completeness script branches on `if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]`. For `workflow_run` events, `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` = "workflow_run" ≠ "push", so it takes the else path — scanning all open PRs. That's correct behavior (same as schedule). Good — no misfire on main. If it had used `GITHUB_REF_NAME` without the event check, it would have tried to scan "main" as if it were a PR branch. It doesn't. ✅

   So the factory logic at this pinned SHA handles the new trigger correctly: workflow_run → else-branch → scan all open PRs + sm-liveness check. 

3. **Run-name**: `run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'` — for workflow_run events, `github.ref_name` is the default branch (main). Fine, cosmetic.

4. **Concurrency**: factory has `group: factory-sm-kicker, cancel-in-progress: false` — runs queue instead of cancelling. With workflow_run added, every Quality completion that happens while a kicker is in-flight just queues another. Kicker jobs are "seconds-cheap watchdogs" — bounded backlog is fine per the factory's own comment.

5. **Event storm cost**: Every Quality completion fires the kicker. Quality runs on every PR push (validation). So every CI finish → kicker run (two tiny jobs on ubuntu-latest, seconds each, often no-ops: "SM alive — nothing to do"). But note: `head-completeness` for the else path scans ALL open PR branches with several API calls per branch (commits, files, check-runs, run lists, + 45s grace sleep when it finds a codeless head). With N open PRs this is a handful of API calls — cheap, and it already runs every 30 min via schedule. Now it also runs on every Quality completion. Modest but acceptable; the payoff (seconds-vs-100-minutes latch latency) is the PR's whole point.

   Actually wait — one more consideration: sm-liveness dispatches machine-sm when no SM run is active. During heavy activity: Quality completes → kicker → SM idle → dispatch tick. machine-sm ticks every 10 min anyway; the kicker just shortens latency. Multiple Quality completions in a burst → multiple kicker runs queued (global concurrency group, no cancel) → sequential dispatches, but each checks liveness first, so at most one redundant dispatch race (two queued kicker runs both see SM idle → double dispatch). The SM tick is guarded by the factory's own `machine-sm` concurrency group, so a second tick queues — the factory comment on machine-sm.yml says "short ticks — the engine idles when busy" and the factory owns the group. Idempotent by design. Not a real issue.

6. **`workflow_run` default-branch requirement**: workflow_run triggers only fire for workflow files on the default branch. This stub will be on main after merge — fine. Note the trigger won't work on the PR branch itself during validation — no harm.

7. **Security**: `workflow_run` events run with the workflow file from the default branch and the token here is `github.token` (permissions: actions write, contents read, PR read, checks read). No untrusted input is interpolated into shell: the factory script uses env vars `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `SM_WORKFLOW` (from pinned inputs), no `github.event.workflow_run.*` fields are used at all in the factory script at this SHA. So no command-injection surface from the new event payload. ✅ Actually, this is worth verifying carefully since `workflow_run` payloads are a classic injection vector — but the factory script never references `github.event` payloads, only API responses via `gh api --jq`. The `sha=$(gh api ... --jq .sha)` values come from the API for branch names enumerated from `gh pr list`. Command injection via a malicious PR branch name? Branch names go into `gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b"` — URL context, and `gh api` treats it as a URL path... A branch name with spaces could break word-splitting, but that's pre-existing factory behavior, unchanged by this PR, and the PR branch names here are repo-controlled-ish. Not in scope of this diff anyway (factory is pinned/frozen; this PR only adds a trigger). And per AGENTS.md this repo's stubs are thin — factory review is out of scope, though I can note it.

8. **Now the redundancy question**: Quality completion now wakes THREE consumers: merge-trigger (factory-merge-trigger), machine-merge (factory-merge), and sm-kicker → machine-sm tick (full SM reconcile). Is the kicker's reaction redundant with merge-trigger? Different jobs: merge-trigger merges pr_approved issues; the SM tick latches the verdict into the SM state machine and decides the next SM action (arm validate/merge, post updates). The incident described is specifically that the SM never latched the green verdict, which merge-trigger doesn't do. So the addition is justified, not duplicate. However there IS overlap in the sense that machine-merge already merges approved PRs on Quality completion — the kicker's contribution is the SM latch. Worth a SUGGESTION-level note at most? Actually the PR description explicitly frames it as the latch fix. Fine.

9. **Parity check**: The stub header says "Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml)". Let me check whether fa's sm-kicker.yml has the same workflow_run trigger (i.e., this is catching up to an established pattern) — quick web fetch. If fa doesn't have it, this repo is pioneering; if it does, parity holds. Let me check flutter_agent_harness? # SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@f0fe78c6225b99ca350f8354af112db937699b61
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    # Frozen machine loop (same freeze contract as machine-sm.yml: agents
    # resolve from dmtools-agents RELEASES by vars.AGENTS_VERSION).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

blocks.text:
Now I have the factory kicker logic at the pinned SHA. Analysis of how it behaves under a `workflow_run` trigger:

1. **`sm-liveness` job**: Checks if machine-sm.yml has an active run; if not, dispatches one. This is payload-independent — reads live repo state via API. Works fine under `workflow_run` trigger. ✅ This is exactly the fix for the described stall: Quality completes → kicker fires → SM idle → dispatch tick → verdict latches within seconds.

2. **`head-completeness` job**: 
   - For `push` events: scans the pushed branch only.
   - Else (schedule, workflow_dispatch, and NOW workflow_run): scans ALL open PR branches. Under `workflow_run` events, `GITHUB_REF_TYPE` is "branch" (default branch) and `GITHUB_REF_NAME` is "main"... wait, careful! For a `workflow_run` event, the workflow run executes on the default branch, so `GITHUB_REF_NAME` = "main" and `GITHUB_REF_TYPE` = "branch".

   ⚠️ **This is a real issue**: the head-completeness script branches on `if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]`. For `workflow_run` events, `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` = "workflow_run" ≠ "push", so it takes the else path — scanning all open PRs. That's correct behavior (same as schedule). Good — no misfire on main. If it had used `GITHUB_REF_NAME` without the event check, it would have tried to scan "main" as if it were a PR branch. It doesn't. ✅

   So the factory logic at this pinned SHA handles the new trigger correctly: workflow_run → else-branch → scan all open PRs + sm-liveness check. 

3. **Run-name**: `run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'` — for workflow_run events, `github.ref_name` is the default branch (main). Fine, cosmetic.

4. **Concurrency**: factory has `group: factory-sm-kicker, cancel-in-progress: false` — runs queue instead of cancelling. With workflow_run added, every Quality completion that happens while a kicker is in-flight just queues another. Kicker jobs are "seconds-cheap watchdogs" — bounded backlog is fine per the factory's own comment.

During heavy activity: Quality completes → kicker → SM idle → dispatch tick. machine-sm ticks every 10 min anyway; the kicker just shortens latency. # SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml.
# Parity with fa (sm-kicker.yml) and dmtools-agents (factory-sm-kicker.yml).
#
# Why dmd needs it: GitHub silently drops schedule() crons on quiet repos —
# dmd's machine-sm.yml ticks were dead 14:44→18:38 on 2026-10-01, which
# parked validated PRs with no live tick to arm validate/merge. The kicker
# re-dispatches machine-sm.yml on its OWN schedule + every non-main push,
# so the state machine keeps moving even when the cron is dropped.
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03): GitHub starved BOTH crons (machine-sm
  # AND this kicker) for 100 minutes on a quiet afternoon — a green
  # validation verdict sat unlatched the whole time and dart#337 stalled
  # until a manual dispatch. Validation verdicts arrive as Quality
  # conclusions; reacting to them closes the gap: latch/merge happens
  # within seconds of the CI finishing, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Quality]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@f0fe78c6225b99ca350f8354af112db937699b61
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
      ci_display_name: Quality
      required_contexts: 'static,gate,agents-gate'

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Now let me understand the context. This is a GitHub Actions workflow change. The PR adds a `workflow_run` trigger to sm-kicker.yml. Let me look at the other workflow files to understand the ecosystem — machine-sm.yml, quality.yml, and check the referenced factory workflow (pinned by SHA).

Key review considerations for `workflow_run` trigger:

1. **Security**: `workflow_run` triggers run in the context of the default branch (main), with the permissions declared in this workflow. This workflow has `actions: write` permission — it re-dispatches machine-sm.yml. The workflow_run event fires for workflows on the default branch... Actually, `workflow_run` fires when a workflow run *concludes* — but only for workflows whose workflow file exists on the default branch. Important nuance: a `workflow_run`-triggered workflow only runs if the workflow file is on the default branch. Since this PR targets main and the file will be on main, that's fine.

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the FROZEN machine loop
# (IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows, reusable).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (version resolution, dmtools install, pack
# run) lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml.
# This file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


permissions:
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510)
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Frozen machine loop — pinned to the immutable SHA of
    # IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows main. Agent code and the dmtools CLI
    # are NOT tied to this SHA: they resolve from RELEASES at run time by
    # repo variables (bump = repo-settings edit, zero workflow changes):
    #   vars.AGENTS_VERSION  — dmtools-agents release tag ('latest' default)
    #   vars.DMTOOLS_VERSION — dmtools-dart CLI release tag ('latest' default)
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — the sm-validation bridge is deleted.
      # gh-315: the sharded agents suite merges in `agents-gate` (the
      # matrix shards themselves are not required contexts, same as `test`).
      validation-checks: '["agents-gate","static","gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-state","asset":"dart-state.json"}'
      # Parallel READ fan-out inside the tick (dmtools-agents#559): wires the
      # Dart runtime's runAsync worker pool into the SM engine — per-PR/issue
      # enrichment + dispatched-CI probes fan out over 4 workers; '0' would
      # take the sequential fallback. Actions stay sequential on the main
      # engine either way.
      parallel-workers: '4'
      # sm_github.json validation rules (validate-armed etc.) dispatch and
      # stamp THIS workflow on PR heads — without it the required contexts
      # (agents-gate/static/gate, produced by quality.yml jobs) never
      # appear and approved PRs stall BLOCKED (issue dmtools-agents#575,
      # live: PR #301 needed a manual Quality dispatch 2026-09-29).
      ci-workflow: quality.yml
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping of github.token
      # arrives EMPTY through a reusable call (live-verified in fa); it
      # rides this INPUT instead (fa machine-sm.yml parity).
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional SILENT_GH_TOKEN), and
    # `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares — mapping a secret the
      # callee does not declare is rejected at call time, a missing
      # declared one fails the guard test.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      # Optional repo secret; unset → empty → the factory falls back to
      # the silent-token input above (github.token), which is the working
      # route for silent updates anyway.
      SILENT_GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SILENT_GH_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).

# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head

name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['Quality']   # the dispatched CI — rename per repo if needed
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')

      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      ci_workflow: quality.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Canonical home for the SM-kicker watchdog every factory repo points at.
# The calling repo keeps a thin stub workflow that calls this one with the
# repo-specific names (defaults match flutter_agent_harness).
#
# Why it exists: a repo whose CI is dispatch-only (no `on.push` on PR
# heads) and whose Machine SM is the sole trigger has two gaps that leave
# a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch one tick.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet strict
#      `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on the new
#      head SHA. Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents,
#      0 files vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch the CI workflow on it.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: Factory SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the Machine SM workflow in the caller repo'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'Workflow display NAME as it appears in the runs API'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check context names'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      sm_workflow:
        description: 'SM workflow file'
        type: string
        default: 'machine-sm.yml'
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'CI workflow file to dispatch'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      ci_display_name:
        description: 'CI workflow display name'
        type: string
        default: 'CI'
      required_contexts:
        description: 'Comma-separated required check contexts'
        type: string
        default: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: sm / ci
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  # Global group, but NO cancel-in-progress (fa #911 diagnosis,
  # 2026-09-25): a push on ANY PR branch used to kill the in-flight kicker
  # for every other branch, leaving sm-liveness/head-completeness
  # check-runs stamped CANCELLED on random heads and polluting PR check
  # rolls repo-wide. The kicker jobs are seconds-cheap watchdogs — let
  # them queue instead of cancelling; a bounded backlog is harmless.
  group: factory-sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
  SM_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.sm_workflow || 'machine-sm.yml' }}
  CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow || 'ci.yml' }}
  CI_DISPLAY: ${{ inputs.ci_display_name || 'CI' }}
  REQUIRED_CONTEXTS: ${{ inputs.required_contexts || 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate' }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/$SM_WORKFLOW/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run "$SM_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          IFS=',' read -ra contexts <<< "$REQUIRED_CONTEXTS"
          jq_ctx=$(printf '%s\n' "${contexts[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq --argjson ctx "$jq_ctx" '[.check_runs[].name | select(. as $n | $ctx | index($n))] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq --arg name "$CI_DISPLAY" '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == $name)] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run "$CI_WORKFLOW" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done
